attributes.location: B2 phase adjacent to B2/C14 interfaces

evidence.quote: the formation of an ordered hcp (D019) phase particles ... was detected. The D019 particles had an irregular shape and precipitated inside the B2 phase adjacent to the B2/C14 interfaces preferentially. According to EDS analysis, the D019 particles were enriched with Ti and Nb but depleted of Cr and Zr; their chemical composition could be expressed as Al28Cr5Nb18Ti45Zr4. The volume fraction of the D019 phase was estimated to be ~3%.
the single-phase bcc Nb30Ti40Zr30 alloy possessed a microstructure with coarse (~150 μm) polygonal grains without any visible chemical heterogeneity (Fig. 3a, b; Table 1)
TEM examination confirmed the B2/C14 Laves phase eutectic structure with an average interlamellar spacing of ~200 nm.

The alloy retained the lamellar morphology (the B2 matrix sliced by the C14 Laves phase lamellae) even after ε ≈50%; however, the lamellae were often bent and/or reoriented along the metal flow direction (Fig. 7d).
At 22 °C, the Nb30Ti40Zr30 alloy exhibited a combination of modest yield strength (675 MPa), excellent compressive ductility (>50%), and pronounced strain hardening capacity (Fig. 6a; Table 2)
The Cr20Nb30Ti40Zr10 alloy demonstrated higher strength (1005 MPa) and strain hardening capacity but much lower compressive ductility (10.9%).
The Al15Cr20Nb15Ti40Zr10 alloy was the strongest (>1700 MPa) among the alloys.
During compression, the alloy yielded at 810 MPa and then rapidly strengthened to the peak value of 1150 MPa
